[[Hofstra Pride men's basketball#Retired jerseys|retired by Hofstra Pride]] }} '''Charles T. Jenkins''' (born February 28, 1989) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He was drafted by the [[Golden State Warriors]] in the [[2011 NBA draft]] after finishing his four-year college career with the [[Hofstra Pride men's basketball|Hofstra Pride]].{{cite web |title=Class Notes 2011 ~ Hofstra Magazine |date=25 January 2012 |publisher=HofstraMagazine.blogspot.com |url=https://hofstramagazine.blogspot.com/2012/01/class-notes-2011.html |access-date=2012-07-18}}{{Cite web |title=Charles Jenkins |work=Player biography |publisher=[[Hofstra University]] |year=2009 |url=http://www.gohofstra.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=22200&ATCLID=3716182 |access-date=13 May 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110811195636/http://www.gohofstra.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=22200&ATCLID=3716182 |archive-date=August 11, 2011}} In addition to being a citizen of the [[United States]], Jenkins also has [[Serbian nationality law|Serbian citizenship]]. While attending [[Hempstead (village), New York|Hempstead]], [[New York (state)|New York]]'s [[Hofstra University]], Jenkins, a {{height|ft=6|in=3}} [[guard (basketball)|guard]] for the [[Hofstra Pride men's basketball|Hofstra Pride men's basketball team]], had already amassed 1,767 points, 440 rebounds, 331 assists and 156 steals through his first three seasons.{{Cite web |title=Charles Jenkins stats |publisher=[[ESPN]] |year=2010 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/6444/charles-jenkins |access-date=13 May 2010}} He is [[Hofstra Pride men's basketball statistical leaders|Hofstra's all-time leading scorer]] (2,463), breaking [[Antoine Agudio]]'s record (2,286) set in 2007–08, and graduated as the second leading scorer in [[Colonial Athletic Association]] history behind [[Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame|Hall of Famer]] [[David Robinson (basketball)|David Robinson]], who scored 2,669 points at [[Navy Midshipmen men's basketball|Navy]].{{Cite news |last=Satriano |first=David |title=Hofstra's Jenkins shows Pride in finale |work=[[New York Post]] |publisher=nypost.com |date=February 27, 2011 |url=http://www.nypost.com/p/sports/college/basketball/jenkins_shows_pride_in_finale_j3EXFwDefT9IDy4t2f8JGJ |access-date=March 6, 2011}} Jenkins had his jersey retired by Hofstra prior to his final home game of his senior season, making him the fourth player in school history to be so honored, and the first to have it retired while still active. ==Early life== Jenkins was born in [[Brooklyn]], New York, where he lived in the [[Brownsville, Brooklyn|Brownsville]] section for six years until moving to [[Rosedale, Queens]].{{cite web |title=Jenkins keeps brother's dream alive all the way to NBA |work=CBS Sports |url=http://www.cbssports.com/nba/story/15256641/jenkins-keeps-brothers-dream-alive-all-the-way-to-nba |access-date=2017-09-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110928201320/http://www.cbssports.com/nba/story/15256641/jenkins-keeps-brothers-dream-alive-all-the-way-to-nba |archive-date=2011-09-28 |url-status=dead}} The youngster took to basketball under the influence of two close family members: his father who had played collegiate ball for the [[Navy Midshipmen men's basketball|Navy]] before transferring to [[Virginia Western Community College]] as well as his older brother who had played some high school basketball.{{cite news|last=Jovanović|first=Miloš|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kuvtTqv5Zws&t=62s|agency=Mondo.rs|title=ŠESTA LIČNA: Čarls Dženkins otvoreno o svemu! (timestamp 01:02)|date=27 March 2020|access-date=15 June 2022}} Teenage Jenkins commuted to [[Holy Cross High School (Flushing)|Holy Cross High School]]{{cite news |title=Hofstra's Jenkins Stayed Home and Stayed Focused |newspaper=NYTimes.com |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2011/03/06/sports/ncaabasketball/06jenkins.html |access-date=2011-03-06 |first=Pete |last=Thamel |author-link=Pete Thamel |date=March 5, 2011}} until transferring to [[Springfield Gardens High School]], where he played high school basketball for three seasons. As a senior in 2005–06, he averaged 21.1 points, 7.2 assists and 5.1 rebounds en route to a ''[[New York Post]]'' selection to the All-New York City Team. ==College career== ===Freshman=== After [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirting]] his [[true freshman]] season of 2006–07, Jenkins began competing for the [[Hofstra University]] [[Hofstra Pride men's basketball|Pride]] in 2007–08. He played in 29 games and averaged 15.0 points and 4.6 rebounds, led his team in free throw percentage (78.0), and finished 10th in the [[Colonial Athletic Association]] (CAA) in scoring (first among freshmen). Jenkins was named the CAA Rookie of the Year, Metropolitan New York Rookie of the Year and to the Third Team All-Metropolitan New York. ===Sophomore=== In 2008–09, Jenkins averaged 19.7 points and 4.8 rebounds in 32 games played. In the last game of the regular season against [[UNCW Seahawks men's basketball|UNC Wilmington]], he surpassed the 1,000-point milestone, joining Agudio as the only two sophomores to reach 1,000 points prior to their junior seasons. At the season's end, his 1,065 points stood 47 points more than Agudio's pace at the end of his respective sophomore season. Jenkins garnered numerous awards for his year. Among them was the coveted [[Haggerty Award]], which is an award given annually to the greater New York Metropolitan area's best [[Division I (NCAA)|Division I]] men's basketball player.{{Cite web |last=Sass |first=Max |title=Charles Jenkins wins second-straight Haggerty Award |publisher=The Chronicle |date=22 April 2010 |url=http://www.hofstrachronicle.com/sports/charles-jenkins-wins-second-straight-haggerty-award-1.1379128 |access-date=13 May 2010 |archive-date=14 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200614083705/http://www.hofstrachronicle.com/sports/charles-jenkins-wins-second-straight-haggerty-award-1.1379128 |url-status=usurped }} He became just the fifth sophomore overall (and first since [[Metta World Peace|Ron Artest]] in 1998–99) to earn it in the 73-year history of the award to that point. ===Junior=== As a junior in 2009–10, Jenkins once again increased most of his season averages. He scored 20.6 points, grabbed 4.5 rebounds, dished out 3.9 assists and shot 40.9% from three-point range. On November 30, 2009, in an 84–80 win versus [[Fairfield Stags men's basketball|Fairfield]], he scored a career-high 38 points on 12-for-17 shooting and went 9-for-9 in free throw attempts. Although the Pride would finish the year with a 19–15 overall record, Jenkins' personal play was good enough to make him the [[Colonial Athletic Association Men's Basketball Player of the Year]].{{Cite web |title=Hofstra's Jenkins Earns CAA Men's Basketball Player of the Year Honors |work=Men's Basketball News |publisher=[[Colonial Athletic Association]] |date=4 March 2010 |url=http://www.caasports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=8500&ATCLID=204901228 |format=Press release |access-date=13 May 2010}} Additionally, he became just the ninth repeat winner of the Haggerty Award.{{Cite web |title=Hofstra's Jenkins Repeats as Haggerty Award winner |work=Men's Basketball News |publisher=[[Colonial Athletic Association]] |date=21 April 2010 |url=http://www.caasports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=8500&ATCLID=204933411 |format=Press release |access-date=13 May 2010}} ===Senior=== Jenkins became just the third player all-time to win the Haggerty Award three times, joining [[Jim McMillian]] ([[Columbia Lions men's basketball|Columbia]], 1968–70) and [[Chris Mullin (basketball)|Chris Mullin]] ([[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]], 1983–85), both of whom later achieved great success at the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] and/or [[Basketball at the Summer Olympics|Olympic]] levels of competition. ==Professional career== ===NBA: Golden State Warriors=== [[File:Charles Jenkins Oct 2012.jpg|thumb|left|Jenkins with the [[Golden State Warriors]] in 2012]] In the [[2011 NBA draft]], combo guard Jenkins was selected in the second round (44th overall) by the [[Golden State Warriors]] after the team had taken shooting guard [[Klay Thompson]] with their first-round pick (11th) earlier in the night.{{cite news |title=Warriors Select Guards Klay Thompson & Charles Jenkins In 2011 NBA Draft |url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/draft_2011_thompson_jenkins_tyler.html |access-date=August 1, 2014 |work=NBA.com |date=June 23, 2011}} Due to the [[2011 NBA lockout]], Jenkins signed with the Italian team [[Teramo Basket]] of the [[Lega Basket Serie A]] on November 24, 2011.{{cite news |last1=Carchia |first1=Emiliano |title=Teramo tabs Warriors draftee Charles Jenkins |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/88998/teramo-tabs-warriors-draftee-charles-jenkins.html |access-date=August 1, 2014 |work=Sportando.com |date=November 24, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160820170731/http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/88998/teramo-tabs-warriors-draftee-charles-jenkins.html |archive-date=2016-08-20 |url-status=dead}} However, the lockout ended within two weeks and he left Teramo without playing any games for the club. On December 9, 2011, he officially signed with the Warriors, coached by [[Mark Jackson]].{{cite news |title=Warriors Sign Second Round Pick Charles Jenkins |url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/jenkinssigned_120911.html |access-date=August 1, 2014 |work=NBA.com |date=December 9, 2011}} Twenty-two-year-old Jenkins made [[2011–12 Golden State Warriors season|his NBA debut]] on December 25, 2011, in the Warriors' [[2011–12 NBA season|2011–12]] season opener against the [[2011–12 Los Angeles Clippers season|Los Angeles Clippers]]. Briefly entering the contest, he finished with one assist in 1 minute of action.{{cite news |title=New-look Clippers open season with road victory over Warriors |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=311225009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170127073520/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=311225009 |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 27, 2017 |access-date=August 1, 2014 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=December 25, 2011}} Settling into the role of fighting for the twenty-three-year-old starting point guard [[Stephen Curry|Steph Curry]]'s backup minutes, rookie Jenkins ended up getting unexpected opportunities towards the end of the [[2011 NBA lockout|lockout]]-shortened season due to the third-year player Curry's persistent [[ankle injury|ankle injuries]].{{cite news |first=Nikhil |last=Dilip |title=Golden State Warriors: How the Addition of Jarrett Jack Helps the Team |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1255381-golden-state-warriors-how-the-addition-of-jarret-jack-helps-the-team |access-date=24 April 2020 |agency=[[Bleacher Report]] |date=11 July 2012}} Though the team had signed [[Nate Robinson]] early into the season to take most of Curry's point guard backup minutes, Jenkins would end up often starting in place of injured Curry. The rookie's minutes especially increased from March 2012, as Curry was ruled out for the rest of the season and [[Monta Ellis]] got traded.{{cite news |first=Zach |last=Buckley |title=Stephen Curry: 3 Reasons Golden State Warriors PG Must Sit Out Until Next Year |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1127052-nba-rumors-3-reasons-warriors-must-move-on-from-stephen-curry |access-date=24 April 2020 |agency=[[Bleacher Report]] |date=31 March 2012}} On March 24, 2012, Jenkins scored career-high 27 points in a 90–87 loss to the Portland Trail Blazers,{{cite news |title=Despite big night by rookie Charles Jenkins, Golden State Warriors lose to Portland Trail Blazers |url=https://www.eastbaytimes.com/2012/03/25/despite-big-night-by-rookie-charles-jenkins-golden-state-warriors-lose-to-portland-trail-blazers/ |access-date=24 April 2020 |agency=[[East Bay Times]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |date=25 March 2012}} continuing to post improved numbers until the end of the season{{cite news |first=Yama |last=Hazheer |title=Golden State Warriors: Charles Jenkins Is Golden for the Warriors |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1154332-four-years-of-college-to-the-pros-charles-jenkins-is-golden-for-the-warriors |access-date=24 April 2020 |agency=[[Bleacher Report]] |date=21 April 2012}} and finishing with an average of 5.8 points and 3.3 assists in 51 games, 28 of them starts. The Warriors failed to make the playoffs; several days after their season ended, the team demoted their GM [[Larry Riley (basketball)|Larry Riley]] to a scouting position while simultaneously promoting the assistant general manager, former [[sports agent|player agent]] [[Bob Myers]], to be the new general manager. Heading into his second season at Golden State, twenty-three-year-old Jenkins participated in the [[2012 NBA Summer League|NBA Summer League]] in [[Las Vegas]] throughout July 2012. Playing alongside Warriors teammates such as rookie [[Harrison Barnes]] and fellow second-year player Klay Thompson, Jenkins had a good showing as the team won each of its five games with Jenkins the top scorer in two of them.{{cite news |first=Marcus |last=Thompson II |title=Charles Jenkins asserts himself in Golden State Warriors' summer league win |url=https://www.mercurynews.com/2012/07/14/charles-jenkins-asserts-himself-in-golden-state-warriors-summer-league-win/ |access-date=24 April 2020 |agency=[[The Mercury News]] |date=14 July 2012}} Just before the Summer League, in anticipation of Robinson leaving, the team had signed point guard [[Jarrett Jack]]{{cite news |first=John |last=Reid |url=https://www.nola.com/hornets/index.ssf/2012/07/new_orleans_hornets_trade_star.html |title=New Orleans Hornets trade starting point guard Jarrett Jack to the Golden State Warriors in three-team deal |agency=[[The Times-Picayune/The New Orleans Advocate]] |date=11 July 2012 |access-date=24 April 2020 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120716051439/https://www.nola.com/hornets/index.ssf/2012/07/new_orleans_hornets_trade_star.html |archive-date=16 July 2012}} with the question of who would be Curry's primary backup in the upcoming season, Jack or Jenkins, initially left open. Once the season began, Jenkins saw his role on the [[2012–13 Golden State Warriors season|team]] diminished severely, getting very little playing time with Curry back healthy and newly-acquired Jack getting most of the backup minutes. On February 21, 2013, Jenkins was traded to the Philadelphia 76ers for a second-round draft pick.{{cite news |title=Warriors Trade Charles Jenkins to Philadelphia |url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/jenkins_trade_022113 |access-date=August 1, 2014 |work=NBA.com |date=February 21, 2013}} ===Philadelphia 76ers=== Joining the [[2012–13 Philadelphia 76ers season|struggling Sixers]], a team well out of the playoff spots and on the verge of [[Tanking (sports)|tanking]] for a better draft position, Jenkins was again relegated to the bench, getting sporadic minutes way down in the pecking order behind guards preferred by head coach [[Doug Collins (basketball)|Doug Collins]] such as [[Jrue Holiday]], [[Evan Turner]], [[Nick Young (basketball)|Nick Young]], [[Damien Wilkins]], and even the newly-acquired [[Justin Holiday]] who joined several weeks after Jenkins.{{cite news |first=Kieran |last=Darcy |title=Charles Jenkins at NBA crossroads |url=https://www.espn.com/new-york/nba/story/_/id/9155338/philadelphia-76ers-charles-jenkins-nba-crossroads |access-date=15 June 2022 |agency=[[ESPN]].com |date=10 April 2013}} At the end of the season, with no firm NBA offers other than several training camp invitations, Jenkins began considering Europe as an option via instructing his agent to pursue those opportunities as well, revealing in later interviews he first got alerted to professional basketball outside the U.S. by fellow Philadelphia benchwarmer [[Jeremy Pargo]] who had explained the [[European professional club basketball system|European club basketball system]] to him during one of their Sixers team flights while offering personal advice "not to settle for an NBA [[Journeyman (sports)|journeyman]] career since there is life in European basketball".{{cite news|last=Jovanović|first=Miloš|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kuvtTqv5Zws&t=776s|agency=Mondo.rs|title=ŠESTA LIČNA: Čarls Dženkins otvoreno o svemu! (timestamp 12:59)|date=27 March 2020|access-date=15 June 2022}} ===Moving to Europe: KK Crvena zvezda=== [[File:Djenka.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Jenkins with Crvena zvezda in December 2013]] On July 30, 2013, following interest from [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] and [[Olimpia Milano]], Jenkins signed a one-year contract with the Serbian team [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]],{{cite news |last1=Ostojić |first1=Aca |title=CRVENA ZVEZDA inks combo guard Jenkins |url=http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2012-13-signings/i/115136 |access-date=August 1, 2014 |work=Euroleague.net |date=July 30, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130803165930/http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2012-13-signings/i/115136 |archive-date=August 3, 2013}}{{cite web |title=Upoznajte Čarlsa Dženkinsa |url=http://www.kkcrvenazvezda.rs/index.php/article/upoznajte-carlsa-dzenkinsa |work=kkcrvenazvezda.rs |access-date=31 July 2013 |language=sr |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130801194203/http://www.kkcrvenazvezda.rs/index.php/article/upoznajte-carlsa-dzenkinsa |archive-date=August 1, 2013}} citing its superior financial offer as his main consideration due to having no specific knowledge of any European clubs. Joining the squad coached by [[Dejan Radonjić (basketball)|Dejan Radonjić]], Jenkins came in alongside a number of acquisitions—including center [[Boban Marjanović]], coveted small forward [[Blake Schilb]], shooting guard [[Jaka Blažič]], and power forward [[Ivan Radenović]]—as the Adriatic League runner-up looked to reinforce on all positions ahead of its return to [[2013–14 Euroleague|Euroleague]] after [[1999–2000 FIBA EuroLeague|14 years]] as well as continuation of the chase for its first [[2013–14 ABA League|Adriatic League]] title domestically. With experienced returning players—point guard [[DeMarcus Nelson]] in his second season with the team, small forward [[Marko Simonović (basketball, born 1986)|Marko Simonović]], and center [[Raško Katić]]—newly-acquired Schilb, coming off a great Euroleague season with [[Élan Chalon]] and signed to a 3-year contract, was projected to lead the team in Euroleague.{{cite news|last=P.|first=V.|url=https://www.novosti.rs/vesti/sport.295.html:440446-Blejk-Silb-pojacao-Zvezdu|agency=[[Večernje novosti]]|title=Blejk Šilb pojačao Zvezdu|date=23 June 2013|access-date=15 June 2022}} With Schilb as the focal point of coach Radonjić's setup initially, Jenkins was mostly coming off the bench while sharing minutes at the two position with Blažič along with occasionally backing up compatriot Nelson at point guard. Drawn in a [[Euroleague 2013–14 Regular Season Group D|Euroleague group]] with [[PBC Lokomotiv Kuban|Lokomotiv Kuban]], [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]], [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]], [[Saski Baskonia|Baskonia]], and [[BC Lietuvos rytas|Lietuvos rytas]], Zvezda failed to progress to the Top 16 Euroleague stage with a 4–6 record that was nevertheless good enough to continue the European season in the second-tier [[2013–14 Eurocup Basketball|Eurocup]]'s [[Eurocup Basketball 2013–14 Last 32 Group L|Last 32 stage]]. With Schilb's suddenly increasingly peripheral role in the team due to not fitting in coach Radonjić's plans all of which eventually led to the player being left off the squad in mid January 2014 and the two sides agreeing a negotiated settlement to break off the 3-year deal after only 6 months,{{cite news|last=M.|first=M.|url=https://sportklub.rs/kosarka/kosarka-ostalo/a49228-zvanicno-silb-napustio-crvenu-zvezdu-i-otisao-u-pariz/|agency=[[Sport Klub]].rs|title=Zvanično: Šilb napustio Crvenu zvezdu i otišao u Pariz|date=29 January 2014|access-date=15 June 2022}} Jenkins saw his minutes increase, scoring team-high 16 points in a Eurocup home win versus [[Bilbao Basket|Bilbao]]. Not long afterwards, by mid-to-late January 2014, he accepted the offer of extending his contract with Crvena zvezda for an additional year with an opt-out clause in the summer transfer window should he receive an NBA offer.{{cite news |last1=Carchia |first1=Emiliano |title=Charles Jenkins officially extends his contract with Crvena Zvezda |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/serbia/110668/charles-jenkins-officially-extends-his-contract-with-crvena-zvezda.html |access-date=August 1, 2014 |work=Sportando.com |date=January 22, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140808051237/http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/serbia/110668/charles-jenkins-officially-extends-his-contract-with-crvena-zvezda.html |archive-date=August 8, 2014 |url-status=dead}} In 2014–15 season, Crvena zvezda won the [[2014–15 ABA League|Adriatic League]] championship, the [[2014–15 Basketball League of Serbia|Serbian League]] championship and the [[Radivoj Korać Cup]]. ===Seasons in Europe=== [[File:Charles Jenkins (basketball) 22 BC Khimki EuroLeague 20180321 (2).jpg|thumb|right|Jenkins with [[BC Khimki|Khimki]] in 2018]] On July 8, 2015, Jenkins signed with Italian club [[Pallacanestro Olimpia Milano|Emporio Armani Milano]] for the 2015–16 season.{{cite news |title=EA7 Emporio Armani adds guard Jenkins |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/66qnsc8m7wyfdei8 |access-date=8 July 2015 |work=Euroleague.net |date=8 July 2015}} On July 15, 2016, Jenkins returned to Crvena zvezda, signing a two-year deal.{{cite news |title=Charles Jenkins returns to KK Crvena Zvezda |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/serbia/206543/charles-jenkins-returns-to-kk-crvena-zvezda.html |access-date=July 16, 2016 |work=Sportando.com |date=July 15, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160820145633/http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/serbia/206543/charles-jenkins-returns-to-kk-crvena-zvezda.html |archive-date=August 20, 2016 |url-status=dead}} In [[2016–17 EuroLeague|2016–17]], he led the [[EuroLeague]] in steals, with 2.1 per game.{{cite news |url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/statistics?agg=PerGame&mode=Leaders&seasonmode=Single&entity=Players&cat=Steals&seasoncode=E2016 |access-date=16 April 2017 |title=Statistics}} Jenkins was also named [[2017 ABA League Playoffs]] [[ABA League Finals MVP|MVP]], where he averaged 12.3 points, 5.3 assists, 3 rebounds, 1.5 steals and average [[Performance Index Rating|PIR]] of 15.2.{{cite news |title=KK Crvena Zvezda crowned again as ABA Liga champions |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/cups/aba-liga/232005/kk-crvena-zvezda-crowned-again-as-aba-liga-champions.html |access-date=16 April 2017 |date=13 April 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170628045715/http://www.sportando.com/en/cups/aba-liga/232005/kk-crvena-zvezda-crowned-again-as-aba-liga-champions.html |archive-date=2017-06-28 |url-status=dead}} On June 29, 2017, Jenkins signed a two-year deal with Russian club [[BC Khimki|Khimki]].{{cite news |title=BC KHIMKI ADDS CHARLES JENKINS |url=http://en.bckhimki.ru/news/clubnews/2017/june/1205/ |access-date=July 4, 2017 |work=bckhimki.ru |date=June 29, 2017}} Jenkins played for HBC Sicklerville in the [[The Basketball Tournament 2018|2018 edition]] of [[The Basketball Tournament]]. He scored 3 points and had 2 rebounds in the team's first-round loss to the Talladega Knights. In the [[2018–19 EuroLeague]] season, he averaged 6.9 points on 42.0% three-point shooting, 2.8 rebounds and 1.0 steal per game over 29 games. On July 5, 2019, Jenkins signed a two-year deal for Crvena zvezda. It is his third stint with the Zvezda.{{cite web |title=Čarls Dženkins po treći put crveno-beli! |url=http://www.kkcrvenazvezda.rs/carls-dzenkins-po-treci-put-crveno-beli-05-07-2019.html |website=kkcrvenazvezda.rs |access-date=5 July 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190705085749/http://www.kkcrvenazvezda.rs/carls-dzenkins-po-treci-put-crveno-beli-05-07-2019.html |archive-date=5 July 2019 |url-status=dead}}{{cite web |title=Zvezda brings back guard Jenkins |url=https://www.euroleague.net/news/i/9s3hciij6tedlnfl |website=euroleague.net |access-date=5 July 2019}} On June 20, 2020, Jenkins signed a contract with Greek club [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]] of the [[EuroLeague]]. ==Personal life== Jenkins has one brother and one sister.
